night_actions: Hoang (Seer) investigated Cong — Result: not a wolf.
Cong (Witch) used SAVE potion on Hoang

day_debate.speaker: Cong
day_debate.statement: Given that no one was killed last night, and I proactively saved Hoang, I propose we focus on establishing clear lines of questioning. I will observe closely for any inconsistencies in statements or behavior.

day_debate.speaker: Riley
day_debate.statement: Cong, you're moving way too fast to 'lead' the questioning. Claiming to be the Witch immediately is a classic wolf move to gain trust and control the narrative. Why are you so eager to establish your authority already? It feels incredibly forced.

day_debate.speaker: Meg
day_debate.statement: Riley is right. Cong, claiming a power role the second the sun comes up is an obvious play for trust. If you're actually the Witch, you're risking your life for no reason; if you're a wolf, you're just trying to steer the vote. It's too reckless.

day_debate.speaker: Riley
day_debate.statement: Look at how Cong is reacting. He's not just claiming a role; he's trying to dictate how we investigate. That's a power play. A real Witch would be cautious, not trying to play puppet master with the whole group. He's too desperate to be trusted.

day_debate.speaker: Nhan
day_debate.statement: Cong's immediate assertion of a leadership role and a claim of Witch status is remarkably hasty. It appears designed to establish control before any investigation has occurred. This feels like a deliberate attempt to manipulate the group.

day_debate.speaker: Riley
day_debate.statement: The fact that Nhan is jumping on the bandwagon so quickly just proves that Cong is the obvious target. Cong, your attempt to play the 'hero' by saving someone is a transparent cover. You're trying to buy loyalty before we even start. Vote Cong.

votes.reasoning: Nhan voted to exile Cong. Reason: Cong’s behavior—immediately claiming a leadership role and a powerful position—is highly suspect. His attempts to dictate the investigation and claim a role prematurely suggest deception and a wolf strategy.

Cong voted to exile Riley. Reason: Riley’s constant accusations and framing of Cong as manipulative are disruptive and designed to derail the investigation. His eagerness to attack Cong’s role is concerning and warrants immediate scrutiny.

Nam voted to exile Cong. Reason: Cong is attempting to establish control and deflect scrutiny. His eagerness to claim a powerful role without investigation warrants immediate exile to prevent further manipulation.

Jin voted to exile Cong. Reason: Cong’s eagerness to claim authority and dictate the process is concerning. His proactive ‘saving’ of Hoang feels like a calculated attempt to gain trust, a classic wolf tactic. I vote to exile him to force transparency.

Hoang voted to exile Cong. Reason: Riley and Meg highlighted Cong’s attempt to establish control and buy loyalty. His haste to claim authority and dictate the investigation aligns with a wolf’s strategy to deceive and mislead the villagers.

Riley voted to exile Cong. Reason: Cong's immediate claim to be the Witch and his attempt to control the group's investigation are huge red flags. It's a textbook attempt to manufacture trust. We can't risk letting a fake power role lead the village.

Meg voted to exile Cong. Reason: Cong's immediate claim to be the Witch is far too aggressive. Real power roles usually wait to see the town's direction before revealing themselves. This feels like a desperate attempt to seize control of the conversation and fabricate trust from the start.

night_actions: Hoang (Seer) investigated Nam — Result: not a wolf.

day_debate.speaker: Riley
day_debate.statement: Nhan's death is a disaster because we lost a voice of reason. Now we're left with Hoang, who survived the first night miraculously. It's too convenient. Hoang, your silence is starting to look like a wolf trying to blend in while the noise happens elsewhere.

day_debate.speaker: Nam
day_debate.statement: Hoang's continued silence is a deliberate tactic. He’s observing, waiting for chaos, and allowing Cong to dictate the narrative. That’s a classic wolf strategy.

day_debate.speaker: Hoang
day_debate.statement: Nam's deflection is a clear indicator of guilt. His attempts to shift blame to the Seer reveal a desire to conceal his actions. I will continue to observe him closely.

day_debate.speaker: Riley
day_debate.statement: Hoang, calling yourself a Seer while Nam is actually speaking up is a pathetic attempt to seize control. This 'observation' act is a shield. You're not observing us; you're calculating how to survive. Your logic is circular and smells like a wolf.

day_debate.speaker: Nam
day_debate.statement: Hoang's deflection, blaming Nam for his silence, is a transparent attempt to divert attention. His continued refusal to engage is precisely the behavior of someone attempting to conceal something.

day_debate.speaker: Riley
day_debate.statement: Hoang, your 'observational' act is a joke. You're not a Seer; you're a wolf using a fake power role to freeze the vote and manipulate us. Nam is the only one actually trying to solve this. It's time we stop letting Hoang play games.

votes.reasoning: Nam voted to exile Hoang. Reason: Hoang's silence is a deliberate tactic to mislead. His deflection of blame to Nam reveals a desire to conceal his actions. We must expose this deception to prevent further manipulation.

Jin voted to exile Nam. Reason: Nam is actively manipulating the discussion and creating confusion. His attempts to discredit the Seer and redirect suspicion are a clear indicator of deception. Exile him to cut off the wolf’s narrative.

Hoang voted to exile Riley. Reason: Riley's relentless criticism of the Seer and his attempts to discredit my investigation suggest he is actively attempting to mislead the village. Exile him to disrupt his manipulative strategy.

Riley voted to exile Hoang. Reason: Hoang's claim to be the Seer is a desperate move to gain immunity. His silence followed by a sudden, vague accusation against Nam is a textbook wolf tactic to deflect suspicion once the village starts closing in on him.

Meg voted to exile Hoang. Reason: Hoang's sudden claim to be the Seer feels like a desperate reaction to Riley and Nam's pressure. A real Seer would have provided more concrete lead-ins. His 'observational' style is just a cover for calculating his next move.
